title: Orchestrator for heterogeneous open-LLM onboarding, deterministic validation, and safe rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a resilient orchestration layer that unifies open-source LLM intake (HF, S3, direct vendor bundles), multi-path conversion (PT -> TorchScript/ONNX/Triton-friendly artifacts), deterministic validation, and automated model-version pin publishing. The orchestrator must produce signed, immutable pins and a performance profile entry in the model catalog with standard metrics (latency p50/p95, throughput at batch sizes, memory/KV cache behavior, token cost estimates). It must support canary rollouts, automated rollback on profile/regression or infra errors, and expose hooks for downstream Dedicated/Private deployment pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Automated intake supports at least HF repo and S3 tarball sources
Conversion pipeline emits runtime-compatible artifacts and artifacts pass sanity checks (dtype, layer shapes, kv-cache warm-up)
Deterministic validation produces reproducible sample outputs across runs and records checksum-based evidence
Model pin is published to model catalog with an associated performance profile (latency p50/p95, throughput for standard batch sizes, memory footprint)
Rollback path exercised in e2e test: if profile regression >10% or infra failure occurs during rollout, system reverts to prior pinned version within SLO
End-to-end onboarding (source -> published profile + pin) completes for medium-sized model (~7B) within 4 hours on CI infra in clean runs
success_metrics: % of community model intakes fully automated: target 80%
Median time to publish profile+pin: <3 hours
Number of rollbacks triggered by automation and correctly executed: target >= 1 drill per quarter
design_notes: We need a thin stateful coordinator that sequences: intake fetch, conversion matrix selection (based on model size/ops), conversion jobs on conversion fleet, deterministic validation (checksum + sample prompts), profile run on a profiling pool, pin signing, and catalog publish. For speed we will reuse lightweight conversion containers and pre-cached kernels for common ops. Consider adopting container snapshots to reduce cold-start time for conversion jobs.
implementation_plan: Phase 0: Spike on multi-source fetch (HF + S3) and build canonical weight ingestion format
Phase 1: Conversion framework: pluggable converters for TorchScript, ONNX, and triton-optimized bundles
Phase 2: Deterministic validation harness and checksum registry
Phase 3: Profiling runner that executes standardized benchmarks and emits profile JSON to catalog
Phase 4: Pin creation, signing, and atomic publish API with rollback metadata
Phase 5: Canary rollout automation and failure-detection rules integrated with runtime routing
open_questions: What level of deterministic output is required for every encoder-decoder vs decoder-only model?
Do we require full bitwise reproducibility or only token-level stable outputs for validation?
Which KMS/HSM flow will sign pins for Private customers vs hosted pins?
How should we store conversion artifacts to support point-in-time rollbacks without inflating storage costs?
risks_and_mitigations: Conversion flakiness across opsets: mitigate via standardized test-suite and pinned converter images
Long-running conversion for very large weights: mitigation is to provide streaming+chunked conversion and early failure detection
Profile variance due to noisy infra: use isolated profiling pool and repeated runs to compute stable percentiles
Security: untrusted community weights may contain malicious code in custom ops — mitigate by sandboxed conversion and static analysis
